title: What RNIT Sells: Identity, Governance, Conversational AI and SaaS

web_blocks.text: RNIT reports one operating segment, not separately measured product businesses. FY2026 describes AI solutions, software development, digital platforms, technology consulting and support; H1 FY2027 describes software development, AI design, development, support and maintenance. Audited product revenue, operating profit, SaaS share, customer concentration and product pricing are not split out. The offerings below are analytical sub-families, not reportable segments. This boundary matters: we can examine real contracts and still cannot assign a percentage of sales or profit to Faceify, NIA, identity or ERP. [1] [2] [3]

web_blocks.takeaway: The product range is broader than the financial disclosure. No line can be assigned a percentage of revenue or profit; the audit baseline remains one combined software-and-services segment. [1] [3]

web_blocks.text: The clearest identity example is the executed SLA with Andhra Pradesh’s Commissionerate of Higher Education. The buyer needed mobile facial recognition to authenticate attendance across government, aided and private colleges. RNIT’s filed scope includes design, development, integration, deployment, user training, technical support and maintenance. The agreement covers about 3,900 institutions and 1.3 million students, staff and users for two years. The transaction price depends on attendance authentications processed; the per-authentication rate and actual billable volume are not disclosed. This is a delivered service scope, not a separate audited product segment. [6]

A second state example extends attendance systems across Telangana higher education, SBTET, collegiate education and ITIs. TGTS work orders describe implementation and maintenance for roughly one million users on a three-year SaaS rate-contract basis. The use case is repeated attendance capture across institutions, but the filing does not state the tariff, number of live users, project margin or amount collected. A large scope can support distribution and references; only active usage, accepted records and cash receipts would establish its economic contribution. [11] An earlier BSE filing from 25 November 2025 described another Telangana Social Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society scope: attendance for approximately 1,70,000 students per day across 268 institutions under SaaS, with usage-based pricing and a two-week go-live target. This is a historical contracted scope, not current activity or a verified paid-user count. [44]

NIA, or Neural Intellectual Assistant, is the clearest conversational-AI offer. A 22 September 2026 Notification of Award from APSSDC describes a multilingual interview and job-preparation platform integrated with Naipunyam and aligned to national skills frameworks. The scope is up to 20 lakh users or interview sessions. Pursuing students may receive two attempts at least three months apart; other users receive one. The service bills per minute per user and provides for five years of services from contract signing. The filing classifies the award Tier 7, above ₹25 crore inclusive of GST, but payment depends on actual usage and satisfactory delivery. Capacity is not completed sessions or recognized revenue. [43]

The APSSDC notice also gives a useful implementation sequence: configuration, integration and deployment are scheduled within 15 working days of the Notification of Award, subject to dependencies and approvals. It describes adaptive interviews, multilingual voice interaction, automated feedback, analytics and competency assessment. The filing does not report go-live acceptance, interview completion, model accuracy, cost per minute or subsequent cash. Treat it as a material awarded project and a test of NIA’s scale, not a result already delivered across the maximum population. [43]

Education administration is a broader workflow than attendance. An APTS award for Andhra Pradesh’s Commissionerate of Collegiate Education covers design, development and maintenance of modules, with a two-month development phase and five years of O&M after deployment. A separate BSE disclosure names an online application to monitor academic and NCVET activities for the State Board of Technical Education and Training. Those are specific department tasks, but no standalone revenue, user fee or renewal is disclosed. [13] [14]

Faceify Edu is management’s productized campus offer for administration, attendance, engagement and operations; Faceify Corp targets workforce, visitors, access and operational workflows. RIMS is positioned as real-time identity capture and authentication. FY2026 describes cloud-native SaaS products for SMEs and institutions, but no customer count, annual recurring revenue, churn, paid seats or support cost is reported. A product name establishes intended functionality, not material adoption. [1] [9] [10]

The company also describes department software, ERP, analytics, IoT-enabled solutions, technology consulting and support. Its audited statement combines these with AI and digital platforms in the same segment. FY2026 consultancy charges of ₹1,460.27 lakh exceeded employee-benefit expense of ₹795.29 lakh; the filing does not define every activity in the consultancy line. This mix may provide flexible implementation capacity, or may indicate customer-specific work. It is a reason to monitor reuse and delivery effort, not proof that all engineering is outsourced. [1]

RNIT’s public procurement route is visible through APTS, APSSDC and TGTS. The APSSDC January filing says RNIT had been declared L1 through an open competitive bidding process; the later September award sets out usage terms. APTSL and TGTS are government undertakings that appear in the filed awards. The public record does not map a reseller, systems integrator, hardware dealer or international channel. Do not invent a distribution network from a contract announcement. [5] [11] [13] [43]

Pricing differs by product and public buyer. The Higher Education FRS SLA is transaction-based per attendance authentication; TGTS uses a SaaS rate-contract structure without a published rate; NIA is usage-linked per-minute-per-user. The APSSDC Tier 7 label signals a value band above ₹25 crore under company policy, not a fixed cash minimum. RNIT’s accounting policy also allows time-and-material, fixed-price, milestone, subscription and managed-service arrangements. No public tariff or recognized revenue split lets us calculate realized unit economics. [1] [6] [11] [43]

The workflow from award to cash has distinct gates: notification, signed agreement, configuration, integration, user testing, customer acceptance, billable usage, invoice, collection and renewal. RNIT’s auditor identifies performance obligations, stage of completion, contract assets, unbilled revenue and acceptance as significant revenue-recognition judgments. The P&L may recognize project progress before cash arrives. Track accepted deployments and post-period receipts, not only announced scope. [1] [3]

Geography is disclosed only in aggregate. FY2026 revenue included ₹3,382.43 lakh domestic and ₹1,767.45 lakh export, compared with ₹2,480.64 lakh and ₹741.95 lakh in FY2025. This establishes an export contribution, not destination or concentration. Government programs may widen references; exports may broaden addressable demand; neither proves a diversified customer base because top-customer exposure and product-level sales are not published. [1]

A common codebase could connect attendance, education administration, identity and NIA, but the reports do not show how many modules share software or how much engineering is reused. The same registered user can generate multiple verification events, so activity totals are not equivalent to unique paid users. In the September NIA award, up to 20 lakh users/interview sessions is an authorized scope; completed sessions and billable minutes remain unreported. Ask for paid active-user cohorts, renewal and service-level outcomes. [1] [3] [7] [43]

The company-authored case-study hub is linked for readers, but its detailed case pages were not retrievable in this research pass. No case-page scale or outcome figure is relied on here. Exchange filings establish the AP attendance, Telangana rate-contract and NIA scopes; audited accounts still do not isolate their revenue, profit, billings or cash. That evidence hierarchy preserves real commercial activity without allowing marketing claims to stand in for audited economics. [6] [8] [11] [43]

For each offering, separate functionality, deployment and unit economics. The FRS agreement identifies a mobile attendance workflow; the Telangana notices add a larger rate-contract scope; NIA identifies a multilingual interview agent and usage model; Faceify is a product direction rather than a reported revenue stream. The missing data are product revenue, renewal, active users, customer concentration, support effort and collections. Until RNIT reports these, use the product families to understand strategy and delivery risk, not to invent a segment mix. [1] [3] [6] [11] [43]

epigraph.quote: Our AI & IOT based comprehensive solutions must deliver real-world impact.
epigraph.author: Raja Srinivas Nandigam, Managing Director’s message, FY2025 annual report [2]

book_paragraphs: You are looking at one software-and-services segment wearing several product names. The names matter because they show where management hopes to reuse technology, but they do not create separate reported businesses. Audited descriptions combine AI, software development, digital platforms, consulting, support and maintenance. Product revenue, profit splits, SaaS share and customer concentration are not published. Your first discipline is to say this directly rather than turn a catalog into a financial segment table. [1] [2] [3]

Start with the attendance workflow in Andhra Pradesh. The buyer is the Commissionerate of Higher Education; the filed SLA covers about 3,900 institutions and 1.3 million students, staff and users. RNIT is to design, develop, integrate and deploy a mobile facial-recognition attendance system, train users and maintain the application. The service price is transaction-based on attendance authentications and the SLA lasts two years. The filing does not publish a rate, accepted volume, error rate, active users or collections. This is a concrete customer example, not proof of unit economics. [6]

The example has an end-to-end shape you can test. A department has an attendance-authentication requirement; RNIT supplies mobile-driven face recognition, integrates it with the department’s systems, deploys it across institutions, trains users and maintains the service. Billing follows authentications processed. What remains unreported is how many users are active, whether each authentication is accepted, how many invoices are paid and what support costs remain. The product may be useful without yet proving a high-margin subscription engine. [6]

Telangana extends the same workflow to higher education, SBTET, collegiate education and ITIs. Work orders through TGTS describe roughly one million users, a three-year period and a SaaS rate-contract arrangement. Implementation and maintenance are explicit, but the monetary rate, actual activity and collections are not. The multi-state footprint is evidence of buyers and scope; it is not evidence that every named user is paying. Ask for active rollouts, monthly authentications, service incidents, contract extensions and the cash collected from this customer. [11]

A historical Telangana Social Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society order supplies another concrete delivery model. RNIT’s 25 November 2025 filing described a facial-recognition attendance system scoped for about 1,70,000 students a day across 268 institutions, provided as SaaS with usage-based consideration and a two-week go-live target. The amount varies with identifications; the notice does not show later active usage or cash collected. The March 2026 TGTS rate-contract scope is a separate filing and should not be added to this one as if the users were unique. [44]

NIA begins with a different user problem: job seekers need to practice interviews, receive feedback and assess skill gaps in multiple languages. APSSDC’s September 2026 award names a multilingual interview and job-preparation platform integrated with Naipunyam. The authorized scope is up to 20 lakh users or interview sessions, with up to two attempts for pursuing students and one for other users. These are product rules, not usage results. Check completed sessions, language mix, quality, human escalation and paid minutes before inferring adoption. [43]

The pricing model is more informative than a headline project tier. The filing says charges are per minute per user, based on actual usage and satisfactory delivery; it also provides for a five-year service term from signing. RNIT classifies the award as Tier 7, above ₹25 crore inclusive of GST, but that is not a fixed guaranteed receipt. A platform can be designed for millions and still generate less cash if sessions are few, the acceptance criteria are unmet or usage costs exceed revenue. [43]

The APSSDC story has a chronology worth keeping. A January filing described the award and said formal execution and performance security remained in process. The later September notice gave the more detailed NIA scope and terms. The filings do not clearly explain whether the second notice amends the first or records a separate contract stage. Do not count both as two independent projects or as two revenue amounts. Ask management for the signed contract value, its minimum commitment and the actual delivery status. [5] [43]

A second AP education workflow covers the Commissionerate of Collegiate Education. APTS awarded modules with two months for development and five years of O&M after deployment. A separate notice describes an online application for academic and NCVET activities for SBTET. These examples show that the company sells more than face matching: it can also build and maintain administrative modules. The public record does not split their revenue, pricing or support margin from the single operating segment. [13] [14]

Faceify Edu and Faceify Corp are the intended standardized offers for campuses and businesses. Edu is described for administration, attendance and student engagement; Corp for workforce, visitor and access workflows. RNIT says they are cloud-native SaaS platforms, but the filings do not disclose paid customer counts, subscription revenue, churn or renewal. A common product might spread engineering costs across customers. Until cohorts and revenue are published, call this a product strategy rather than a proven recurring-revenue base. [1] [9] [10] A historical Telangana Social Welfare order is another filed example of that model, but its 2025 user scope is not a current utilization count. [44]

The case-study hub is available as a link, but its detailed pages were not retrievable in this research pass. We therefore do not rely on the claimed scope of its other case studies. This restraint matters: a company-authored success story can help you generate diligence questions, but it is not a substitute for an exchange filing, customer confirmation or audited receivable. The strongest external evidence here is the filed scope and named counterparty; the unresolved question is what was accepted and collected. [6] [8] [11]

Geography is visible only in aggregate. Domestic revenue was ₹3,382.43 lakh and export revenue ₹1,767.45 lakh in FY2026, up from ₹2,480.64 lakh and ₹741.95 lakh in FY2025. The numbers show material export contribution, but not which countries, customers or products supplied it. A rising export line can broaden demand; a small number of large contracts can still leave concentration high. Do not describe the company as diversified until customer-level reporting supports that conclusion. [1]

The accounting policy names time-and-material, fixed-price, milestone, subscription and managed-service arrangements. Each changes the order of cash and risk. Fixed-price software can suffer cost overruns; milestone work waits for customer approval; subscription billing can be repeatable but only if the buyer renews; managed services can continue while requiring support. The accounts do not disclose the mix, so you cannot choose one average billing cycle or one price-per-seat model for all products. [1] [3]

Public procurement is visible through APTS, APSSDC and TGTS, but the vendor route beyond those agencies is not mapped. APSSDC’s earlier notice described an open competitive process and RNIT as L1; the later award identifies the service terms. The accounts say some contracts can include subcontractor services or third-party equipment. This means the delivery chain can involve more actors than the product brand suggests. Ask whether RNIT controls the software, acts as prime contractor, resells components or coordinates specialists on each project. [1] [5] [11] [43]

The customer examples also have different acceptance gates. An attendance system needs reliable face capture, exception handling and departmental integration; an interview platform needs language quality, safe escalation and useful assessment; an administrative module needs data migration and staff training. A successful attendance deployment does not validate NIA’s unit cost, and a high interview-session ceiling does not prove Faceify adoption among SMEs. Keep the customer, product, billable unit and renewal outcome linked in each diligence note. [6] [13] [43]

A project ledger would make the business much easier to underwrite. For each contract, report award date, signed value or usage formula, user scope, planned go-live, acceptance, amount invoiced, amount collected, cost to serve and renewal. The filings provide pieces of that chain, such as a transaction pricing unit in attendance and a per-minute fee in NIA, but not the whole bridge. It is possible that the economics are attractive; the market cannot test it from a single aggregated segment. [1] [3] [6] [43]

The portfolio can be coherent and still have unclear economics. Identity may open a government account, education modules may add workflows, NIA may add a new interface, and Faceify may target business subscriptions. The same engineering foundation might serve multiple buyers, or every deployment may require substantial customization. The FY2026 consultancy expense and one-segment disclosure leave both explanations open. Your conclusion should therefore recognize the named customer work and leave product-level margins unassigned until RNIT reports them. [1] [2]

A blank product-mix table is not a failure of analysis. It is a map of information risk. RNIT reports one operating segment, so no revenue or profit share can be assigned to identity, education, NIA, Faceify or ERP. The BSE notices establish real customer scopes; the accounts do not disclose how much each contributes. If later filings publish renewal, active-user and project-cash data, you can move from describing a portfolio to judging a product engine. Until then, do not mistake scale of potential use for value captured. [1] [2] [3]

The Higher Education FRS example lets you follow the service more closely. A department authorizes deployment across colleges; RNIT builds a mobile capture workflow, integrates it with the department’s attendance environment, trains users and maintains the system under the SLA. Authentication events are the billing unit. The agreement states a two-year term and population scope, but not accepted event counts, rate per authentication or cash received. Do not turn the 1.3 million user scope into 1.3 million paying subscriptions. [6]

The NIA user journey is similarly bounded. A student or job seeker enters the state skill portal, completes a multilingual interview simulation and receives feedback or a skill-gap assessment. RNIT’s award describes adaptive interviews, voice interaction and analytics; the usage ceiling is 20 lakh users or sessions, with attempt limits for different cohorts. Billing is per minute per user and depends on actual use and satisfactory delivery. The platform could scale cheaply if the model and content generalize; cost per session, language accuracy and repeat demand remain undisclosed. [43]

Telangana’s newer education work order and the earlier Social Welfare Society scope illustrate two forms of public-sector expansion. The March 2026 TGTS order covers about one million users across several higher-education bodies for three years; the November 2025 Society filing scoped attendance for 1,70,000 students per day across 268 institutions under usage-based SaaS. These are separate programs and must not be added as unique users or recurring revenue without reconciliation. They do show that state agencies specify populations and service terms; they do not show that every scoped user became active. [11] [44]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — product labels are not revenue segments
book_callouts.text: A catalog can show what management hopes to sell repeatedly. Only renewals, paid usage and cash disclosures show whether the catalog has become a scalable business.
